name: FL-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Patronis's massive financial advantage ($3.8M raised vs $174K)
model.rationale: This deep-red Florida Panhandle seat has an R+18 lean, and incumbent Jimmy Patronis holds an overwhelming fundraising edge with substantial outside support, while Democrat Gay Valimont has raised little. Prediction markets price the race around 95% Republican, consistent with a Safe R rating.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Valimont within single digits, or a major scandal involving Patronis, would be the main signals of a shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Florida's 1st District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with an 18-point Republican advantage in recent partisan performance. Jimmy Patronis, the incumbent, is running for a full term after winning the seat in a special election and has renominated without difficulty.

Patronis has raised nearly $3.8 million and holds over $930,000 in cash, backed by more than $2 million in outside spending. Democrat Gay Valimont has raised about $174,000 with minimal outside help. No public polls cover the race, but prediction markets give Patronis roughly a 95% chance of winning. The fundamentals, money, and district lean all point to a comfortable Republican hold.
